articleTitle: Use of Earth observation data in agribusiness
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Systems for European Markets - Looking to the Next Millennium (Digest No. 1997/024)
abstract: The application of Earth observation to agricultural monitoring has been a growing field. In Europe the MARS programme (Monitoring Agriculture by Remote Sensing), sponsored by the European Commission, has done much to develop the field and bring it from a research curiosity to operational status for monitoring agricultural fraud within the Common Agricultural Policy and providing inputs to the generation of agricultural statistics. The technology also offers potential within a variety of agribusinesses where it can make a cost effective contribution in decision making processes. This paper illustrates the use of Earth observation data in agribusiness by giving examples from Logica's portfolio of applications. Two different applications are discussed in detail: a yield prediction, with particular reference to sugar beet; and a land cover classification, with particular reference to UK potato crop monitoring.

articleTitle: Satellite synthetic aperture radar data-capability and prospects
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Systems for European Markets - Looking to the Next Millennium (Digest No. 1997/024)
abstract: Satellite-based radar systems have been collecting data of the Earth's surface for some time. Prominent in this area are the ERS series of satellites, operated by the European Space Agency (ESA), which have been imaging the world for over five years. Within this period, many potential applications of the data have been found but the full economic benefits of the sensor are still being realised. This paper explores a number of applications, with a particular focus on the mapping and monitoring of land features, where satellite radar systems have a future, both in terms of offering a unique source of information and a back-up where other, more appropriate, sources of data are available. In particular the author discusses agriculture, forestry, oil and gas exploration, urban mapping and development.

articleTitle: Sirius 2: European-wide satellite services from GE
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Systems for European Markets - Looking to the Next Millennium (Digest No. 1997/024)
abstract: In 1994, General Electric (GE) took the strategic decision to provide satellite communications services outside their traditional market in the US. GE Capital Satellites International was established to build on the experience and resources of GE Americom and provide a full range of satellite communications services in the European, African, and Asia-Pacific regions. The company's first venture is in Europe, where from late 1997 GE Capital Satellites Europe will provide European-wide services via the new Sirius 2 Ku-band satellite owned and operated jointly with NSAB of Sweden. The author discusses the characteristics of this satellite, the market it is aimed at and applications.

articleTitle: Developing digital technology for satellite applications in the next millenium
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Systems for European Markets - Looking to the Next Millennium (Digest No. 1997/024)
abstract: This paper reviews EUTELSAT's approach for the preparation of its satellite constellation, in particular the Hot Bird constellation at 13/spl deg/ East, to support digital broadcasting as well as to cope with a range of new applications for the next millenium. The EUTELSAT Hot Bird satellites (numbered 1 to 5), which will be co-located at 13/spl deg/ East, operate over the whole 10.7-12.75 GHz band on the downlink, and, together will provide about 100 transponders for analogue and digital TV services.

articleTitle: EAST and other applications for future European telecommunications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Systems for European Markets - Looking to the Next Millennium (Digest No. 1997/024)
abstract: This paper examines the likely developments in satellite telecommunications in Europe in the early years of the 21st century. The paper identifies the main spacecraft design drivers for mobile, rural telephony and wideband applications, with a particular focus on EAST (Euro-African Satellite Telecommunications) and WEST (Wideband European Satellite Telecommunications), the major Matra Marconi Space initiatives for mobile, rural telephony and wideband satellites to ensure a European option competing with the US industry initiatives.

articleTitle: ATM performance of existing EUTELSAT systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Systems for European Markets - Looking to the Next Millennium (Digest No. 1997/024)
abstract: This paper investigates the use of currently available EUTELSAT satellite transmission systems as an immediate solution for the deployment of early ATM services. It describes the results of rests and trials of ATM transmissions on EUTELSAT satellites using TDMA for purposes of validating the quality of satellite channels carrying ATM traffic.

articleTitle: Satellite systems for operational meteorology and climatology
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Systems for European Markets - Looking to the Next Millennium (Digest No. 1997/024)
abstract: Operational weather forecasting has benefited operationally from observations from space for nearly twenty years. International collaboration is strong and increasing. Europe is developing its observation programmes, in close cooperation with the US, and seeks wider collaboration, ultimately on a global basis. The author discusses the role of remote sensing satellites in meteorology.

articleTitle: Europe's role in the next millennium towards the development of the next generation of global navigation satellite systems (GNSS)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Systems for European Markets - Looking to the Next Millennium (Digest No. 1997/024)
abstract: This paper studies the state-of-the-art in time and frequency technologies: future clocks, time-transfer and time-dissemination techniques, and their application towards the next-generation of global navigation satellite systems. The requirement for an upgrade to GPS is discussed, and the potential opportunities for European industry are discussed with an identification of key future market areas. We briefly describe the exciting developments towards a seamless, international, wholly-civil GNSS, and show the importance of frequency-band allocation issues in defining the GNSS system architecture. It is concluded that 10 millimetre real-time position determination and 30 picosecond time-transfer capability is technologically achievable, but that the political and institutional issues must first be resolved.
